title: Long-Term Quality Of Life And Symptom Assessment Among Recurrence-Free Patients Who Underwent Cytoreductive Surgery and Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy
official: Long-Term Quality Of Life And Symptom Assessment Among Recurrence-Free Patients Who Underwent Cytoreductive Surgery and Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy
summary: To evaluate long-term quality of life (QoL) and participant reported symptom burden in disease-free survivors who have undergone cytoreductive surgery with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (CRS/HIPEC) at MD Anderson, with primary emphasis on overall (composite) QoL as measured by validated instruments.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Males and females; age ≥18 years at the time of enrollment
2. Underwent curative-intent CRS/HIPEC at MD Anderson for gastrointestinal malignancies, including colorectal cancers, appendiceal cancers, and peritoneal mesothelioma between March 1, 2016, and June 30, 2025
3. Had a complete cytoreduction with a completeness of cytoreduction score (CC) of 0 or 1
4. Currently alive and at least 6 months disease-free post-CRS/HIPEC, based on clinical documentation and follow-up imaging
5. English-speaking
6. Capable of completing an electronic survey (via REDCap)
7. Provides informed consent by proceeding to survey commencement

Exclusion Criteria:

* 1\. Evidence of recurrent or active malignancy at time of chart review 2. Underwent CRS/HIPEC for non-malignant conditions (e.g., multicystic mesothelioma, well-differentiated papillary mesothelioma) 3. Underwent palliative-intent surgery or had an incomplete cytoreduction (CC-2 or CC-3) 4. Did not receive HIPEC (CRS only) 5. Received HIPEC on a clinical trial 6. Significant cognitive impairment limiting ability to provide informed consent or complete the survey 7. Non-English-speaking (due to lack of validated translations for study instruments) 8. No valid contact information or no access to electronic communication (e.g., participant portal or email)
